newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea says U.N. officials term drought 'serious'.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea says U.N. officials term drought 'serious'.

text.p: The official media in famine-stricken North Korea on Monday quoted visiting U.N. officials as saying damage in drought-hit areas was "serious" and even rain could not save the harvests.

"They (United Nations officials), accompanied by management officials of cooperative farms, went round maize fields and admitted that drought damage was serious," the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported.

"Dr. Christin Roberto (adviser to U.N.'s Food and Agriculture Organisation) said that he witnessed the heavy loss caused by the drought, adding that harvest cannot be expected even if it rains in the future," KCNA said in a report monitored in Tokyo.

KCNA said the U.N. officials, including Cheryl Ann Hairston of the U.N.'s Development Programme and Charles Schlegel of the U.N. Children's Fund, as well as officials of international missions, visited drought-hit areas on Saturday to study the damage caused by the drought.
Communist North Korea said on Friday that a heatwave and a subsequent drought were having a "catastrophic" impact on its economy and worsening food shortages there.

What it has called an "unprecedented" drought struck as it was struggling to survive widespread famine caused by floods that devastated much of the country's farmland and industrial bases in 1995 and 1996.
North Korea has reported major crop damage from the drought in four of its nine provinces.
International aid agencies have stepped up food appeals for the Stalinist state, warning of imminent starvation, particularly among young children, who are most at risk.
The Rome-based U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) launched a fresh appeal earlier this month for $46 million in food aid for North Korea on top of an earlier request for $95.5 million.
